findings.summary: commit() now sends the *quote response's* cycle instead of the live cycle toggle, so a commit fired before (or after a failed) re-quote subscribes on the wrong billing cycle.
findings.detail:
REGRESSION introduced by this diff. Old code (git diff, same file): `subscribe.mutate({ planKey: selected, cycle }, ...)` — `cycle` is the live `React.useState<Cycle>` at line 49. New code: `dispatchPlanChange(preview, ...)` (line 137) and `apps/web/lib/api/billing.ts:282` `mutations.subscribe({ planKey: preview.planKey, cycle: preview.cycle })`. `preview` is the QuoteResult, and `apps/api/src/billing/proration.service.ts:77,131` echoes back the cycle of the REQUEST, so `preview.cycle` is whatever cycle the last *successful* quote was for.

The re-quote on a cycle toggle is fire-and-forget (lines 72-76, `React.useEffect(..., [cycle])` -> `quote.mutate(..., { onSuccess: applyPreview })`, no onError) and the commit button's `disabled` (lines 286-288) is `isCommitting || changeAction === "NOOP" || (needsDowngradeAck && !ackDowngrade)` — `quote.isPending` is deliberately NOT in it (contrast line 218, where the per-plan Choose button IS gated on `quote.isPending && isSel`). The cycle pills (lines ~diff, `onClick={() => setCycle(c)}`) are not disabled either.

Failure scenario: TRIAL tenant on /choose-plan picks SCALE -> quote(MONTHLY) resolves, summary + button render. Tenant clicks the ANNUAL pill, then clicks `Subscribe to Scale` before the ANNUAL quote returns (or the quote 500s — there is no onError, so `preview` is simply never replaced and nothing tells the user). `commit()` -> SUBSCRIBE branch -> POST /billing/subscribe `{planKey:'SCALE', cycle:'MONTHLY'}`. `subscribe()` writes `cycle: 'MONTHLY'`, `periodEnd = addCycle(now,'MONTHLY')` and `basePriceSnapshot`. The tenant selected Annual (10x price, 12-month period) and gets Monthly; the pre-diff code would have sent 'ANNUAL'. The same staleness applies to `preview.planKey` (line 278/280/282) and to `changeAction` itself, e.g. a tenant on ANNUAL SCALE who quotes MONTHLY SCALE (action=SUBSCRIBE + cycle warning), toggles back to ANNUAL, and commits before the re-quote lands: subscribe() resets periodStart/periodEnd onto a MONTHLY cycle — the exact period reset B58 exists to prevent, now via the chooser's own staleness.

The new unit test pins the stale behaviour as correct: apps/web/lib/api/billing.test.ts:67 "routes SUBSCRIBE to the subscribe mutation with the quoted cycle" — so no gate catches this.
findings.fixHint: Either add `quote.isPending` to the commit button's `disabled` and clear `preview` when `cycle`/`selected` change (so a stale quote can never be committed), or have dispatchPlanChange take the live `{planKey: selected, cycle}` for the SUBSCRIBE branch and assert `preview.planKey === selected && preview.cycle === cycle` before committing.
findings.decision: The diff replaces the live cycle state with the last successful quote's echoed cycle while leaving the cycle re-quote fire-and-forget (no onError) and the commit button enabled during quote.isPending; a commit after a toggle but before (or after a failed) re-quote subscribes on a cycle the toggle no longer shows. That is a money-path regression introduced by this change, not a pre-existing hazard.

findings.summary: applyScheduledDowngrades has no tenant status / deletedAt filter, so a churned, suspended or soft-deleted tenant's armed downgrade still fires and books a second MRR delta on top of the churn delta.
findings.detail:
Line 124-125: `where: { downgradeEffectiveAt: { not: null, lte: now }, downgradeToPlanKey: { not: null } }` — no `tenant: { status: ..., deletedAt: null }`. Its two siblings in the same file both have one: `applyScheduledCancellations` (line ~219) filters `tenant: { status: "ACTIVE", deletedAt: null }`, and `expireTrials` (line ~57) filters `deletedAt: null`. The sweep then unconditionally rewrites `planKey`, `currentPlan`, `basePriceSnapshot`, `Tenant.plan`, deactivates OPERATOR/DRIVER rows, and emits PLAN_CHANGED with `amountDelta` (lines 150-208).

This was inert before this diff because nothing in the product armed `downgradeToPlanKey`: `git grep -n 'useDowngrade' HEAD -- apps/web` returns nothing outside lib/api/billing, and a repo-wide grep for `subscription/downgrade` finds only the controller, the specs and the new chooser code. This change is the first product caller, so the filter gap becomes live with it.

Failure scenario: ACTIVE tenant on SCALE ($499) uses the new chooser to schedule a downgrade to STARTER ($99) effective 2026-10-01 (their periodEnd). On 2026-09-20 their card fails; `billing.service.ts` `suspendOverdueTenants` books the churn via `transitionAndEmit(..., -1, SUBSCRIPTION_SUSPENDED)` = -(499 + addons - discount) and sets status SUSPENDED. On 2026-10-01 at 02:00 `applyScheduledDowngrades` still selects the row (no status filter), applies the downgrade to a non-paying tenant and emits PLAN_CHANGED `amountDelta = roundMoney(99 - 499) = -400`. MRR is Sigma(amountDelta) per the service docblock, so the rollup now understates the run-rate by $400 permanently and never self-heals. Same double-book via `onSubscriptionDeleted` (status CANCELLED, -MRR emitted) followed by the 02:00 sweep, and the same sweep will deactivate a soft-deleted tenant's operators/drivers.
findings.fixHint: Add `tenant: { status: "ACTIVE", deletedAt: null }` to the where-clause (matching applyScheduledCancellations), and decide explicitly what should happen to a schedule left on a tenant that stopped paying — most likely clear the markers rather than apply them.
findings.decision: applyScheduledDowngrades queries only on the marker fields while both siblings in the same file filter on tenant status/deletedAt, and this change is the first product path that arms those markers — so a churned or soft-deleted tenant's schedule now fires, rewrites the plan row, deactivates staff and books a second MRR delta over the churn delta. Newly reachable, therefore in scope.

findings.summary: activateManualSubscription (and updatePlan) reset the billing period / plan without clearing downgradeToPlanKey, downgradeEffectiveAt or retainedUserIds, so the 02:00 cron silently reverses the admin's action and can deactivate every operator and driver.
findings.detail:
`activateManualSubscription` (lines 516-538) upserts `periodStart: now`, `periodEnd: now + billingPeriodDays`, and explicitly `cancelAtPeriodEnd: false` — it disarms ONE transition and leaves the other three fields (`downgradeToPlanKey`, `downgradeEffectiveAt`, `retainedUserIds`) untouched. `updatePlan` (lines 436-450) writes `currentPlan`, `planKey`, `planVersionId`, `basePriceSnapshot` and emits its own PLAN_CHANGED, and clears nothing at all.

The new code asserts the opposite as an invariant: apps/api/src/billing/subscription-mutation.service.ts:99-100 — "At most ONE transition is ever armed: every committing path clears the markers the others write." These two platform-admin writers are committing paths that do not.

Failure scenario (activateManualSubscription): tenant on SCALE schedules a downgrade to STARTER through the new chooser -> `downgradeToPlanKey='STARTER'`, `downgradeEffectiveAt = 2026-10-01`, `retainedUserIds = []` (billing.ts:280 always sends `[]`). The tenant then pays by bank transfer and an admin runs manual activation on 2026-10-05: `periodStart = 2026-10-05`, `periodEnd = 2026-11-05`, `cancelAtPeriodEnd=false`, status ACTIVE. `downgradeEffectiveAt` is still 2026-10-01 — now in the PAST. At the next 02:00 tick `applyScheduledDowngrades` matches (`lte: now`), overwrites `planKey`/`Tenant.plan` to STARTER, rewrites `basePriceSnapshot` to 99, emits PLAN_CHANGED, and — because `retainedUserIds` is `[]` and the team exceeds STARTER's `seatsIncluded` — `updateMany` sets every ACTIVE OPERATOR and DRIVER to INACTIVE (lines 166-197). The admin has no surface that shows or clears the armed schedule.

Same shape via updatePlan: support moves a tenant back up to SCALE after they change their mind; the stale schedule drops them to STARTER at 02:00 on the effective date and books a second PLAN_CHANGED delta against the admin's own.
findings.fixHint: Clear `downgradeToPlanKey`, `downgradeEffectiveAt` and `retainedUserIds` alongside `cancelAtPeriodEnd: false` in activateManualSubscription's update branch, and in updatePlan's subscription upsert; or centralise a `disarmScheduledTransitions(tx, tenantId)` helper the invariant docblock can actually point at.
findings.decision: The new service states the invariant 'every committing path clears the markers the others write', and activateManualSubscription/updatePlan are committing writers that clear at most cancelAtPeriodEnd; an armed chooser downgrade survives an admin re-plan and the 02:00 cron reverses it and deactivates OPERATOR/DRIVER rows. Real by the change's own contract.

findings.summary: The Stripe webhook writers arm cancelAtPeriodEnd without clearing the downgrade markers (and overwrite cancelAtPeriodEnd on every subscription.updated), breaking the exact both-armed hazard cancel()'s own docblock defends against.
findings.detail:
`onSubscriptionDeleted` (lines 644-682) ends with `this.prisma.tenantSubscription.update({ ..., data: { cancelAtPeriodEnd: true } })` and never touches `downgradeToPlanKey`/`downgradeEffectiveAt`/`retainedUserIds`. `onSubscriptionUpdated` (lines 684-703) writes `periodStart`, `periodEnd` and `cancelAtPeriodEnd: subscription.cancel_at_period_end` on every `customer.subscription.updated` and likewise never touches the downgrade markers.

The self-service twin knows this is dangerous: subscription-mutation.service.ts `cancel()` lines 635-644 clear `downgradeToPlanKey`/`downgradeEffectiveAt`/`retainedUserIds` with the comment "A cancellation SUPERSEDES any scheduled downgrade — leaving one armed would let applyScheduledDowngrades re-price the row (rewriting basePriceSnapshot) before applyScheduledCancellations books the churn delta from it, so the negative MRR delta would depend on which cron ran first." The Stripe path leaves precisely that hole, and it is only now reachable because this diff is the first product caller of downgrade().

Failure scenario A (both armed): tenant on SCALE schedules a downgrade to STARTER for 2026-10-01 via the chooser. On 2026-09-20 Stripe deletes the subscription -> `onSubscriptionDeleted` sets tenant CANCELLED, books -(basePriceSnapshot 499 + addons - discount) once, and sets `cancelAtPeriodEnd: true` on a row that still carries `downgradeToPlanKey='STARTER'`. On 2026-10-01 `applyScheduledDowngrades` (no status filter — see the sibling finding) rewrites `basePriceSnapshot` to 99 and books another PLAN_CHANGED delta of -400 for a tenant already churned.

Failure scenario B (the new KEEP_CURRENT classifier): `planChangePreview` (lines 379-412) keys KEEP_CURRENT on `priorSub.downgradeToPlanKey != null || priorSub.cancelAtPeriodEnd`. Because `onSubscriptionUpdated` overwrites `cancelAtPeriodEnd` from Stripe's value on any subscription update (a cycle roll, a price sync, an item add from addon.service), a tenant who cancelled through RouteFlow can have the flag silently flipped back to false — the settings page's cancellation banner and the chooser's "Keep current plan" undo both disappear, and the cancellation is never applied.
findings.fixHint: In onSubscriptionDeleted, clear downgradeToPlanKey/downgradeEffectiveAt/retainedUserIds in the same update that sets cancelAtPeriodEnd. For onSubscriptionUpdated, decide whether Stripe is authoritative for cancelAtPeriodEnd at all (a locally-scheduled cancel is not represented in Stripe), and at minimum do not silently clear a locally-armed flag.
findings.decision: onSubscriptionDeleted arms cancelAtPeriodEnd and onSubscriptionUpdated overwrites it from Stripe on every event, neither touching the downgrade markers — recreating exactly the both-armed, cron-order-dependent MRR delta that cancel()'s docblock says it clears the markers to prevent, and letting Stripe re-arm a cancellation that downgrade()/upgrade() just disarmed.

findings.summary: For a custom-priced (ENTERPRISE) source the new DOWNGRADE route promises "$0 due today" while the period-end cron books a POSITIVE MRR delta and leaves priceOverrideMonthly in place, so the tenant keeps being billed the enterprise rate on the cheaper plan.
findings.detail:
An ACTIVE tenant on ENTERPRISE (planKey='ENTERPRISE', `basePriceSnapshot`/`priceOverrideMonthly` = their negotiated fee, e.g. 2000 — see platform-admin.service.ts:417 `definition.monthlyPrice ?? priorSub?.priceOverrideMonthly ?? null`) picks SCALE on /choose-plan. `planChangePreview` reaches the DOWNGRADE branch (rank 3 -> 2) and returns `proratedNow: null, effectiveAt: periodEnd`; the page renders "Due today $0" (choose-plan/page.tsx summary, `changeAction === 'DOWNGRADE' ? 0 : ...`) and "Takes effect <date>". `downgrade()` (lines 571-626) has no isCustom guard and schedules it.

Then billing-cron.service.ts `applyScheduledDowngrades`:
- line 150-153: `amountDelta = roundMoney(this.planMonthly(version,'SCALE') - this.planMonthly(version,'ENTERPRISE'))`. `planMonthly` (lines 46-50) returns 0 when `monthlyPrice == null`, and ENTERPRISE is `isCustom` with a NULL catalog price — so the ledger receives **+499 on a downgrade** instead of -1501. Sigma(amountDelta) overstates MRR by ~$2,000 permanently.
- line 158: `basePriceSnapshot: targetDef?.monthlyPrice ?? null` overwrites 2000 with 499, so the MRR snapshot now prices the tenant at 499.
- Nothing on this path clears `priceOverrideMonthly`. Both price resolvers prefer it: subscription.service.ts:43-47 (`monthlyPrice = sub.priceOverrideMonthly ?? def.monthlyPrice`) and platform-pricing.service.ts:93-115 (`if (overrideMonthly != null ...) return { monthly: overrideMonthly, source: 'override' }`, which is what drives Stripe price sync).

Net: after the downgrade applies, /settings/billing shows the tenant $2,000/mo on the SCALE plan, `resolveTenantPricing` keeps returning 2000, the MRR snapshot says 499, and the ledger moved +499. The chooser told them $0 due today and a move to the $499 plan.

Honest scoping: subscribe() had the same +delta arithmetic (line 307 nets against `oldPlanMonthly` = 0 for ENTERPRISE) and also never cleared the override, so the arithmetic error is not newly introduced. What IS new is that this route affirmatively renders "$0 due today / takes effect <date>" for a custom-priced tenant, and that the change moves this traffic onto the cron path, which additionally rewrites basePriceSnapshot away from the negotiated fee.
findings.fixHint: Refuse a plan change out of a custom/isCustom plan self-service (route to sales, like subscribe()/upgrade() already do for isCustom targets), or make the cron price the source from `basePriceSnapshot`/`priceOverrideMonthly` when the catalog has no monthlyPrice and clear `priceOverrideMonthly` when leaving a custom plan.
findings.decision: For an isCustom ENTERPRISE source the DOWNGRADE branch has no guard, the preview promises $0 due today, and the cron's planMonthly(ENTERPRISE) is 0 (null catalog price) so amountDelta is booked positive while priceOverrideMonthly is left in place — the ledger and the tenant's actual charge both go wrong. Money-path defect on a route this change opened.

findings.summary: The DOWNGRADE and UPGRADE preview branches silently revoke a pending cancellation, while the KEEP_CURRENT branch one block above warns for the identical state.
findings.detail:
`planChangePreview` selects `cancelAtPeriodEnd` (line 380) and uses it in exactly one of its four branches: the same-plan KEEP_CURRENT branch (line 404-411) returns `warning: "A scheduled change is pending — keeping your current plan cancels it."`. The UPGRADE branch (434-450) and the DOWNGRADE branch (452-488) never look at it, yet both committing paths disarm it: `upgrade()` line 546 `cancelAtPeriodEnd: false` (comment lines 541-545) and `downgrade()` line 614 `cancelAtPeriodEnd: false` (comment lines 612-613 "scheduling a downgrade replaces a pending cancellation rather than stacking on top of it").

Failure scenario: a tenant cancels from /settings/billing (`cancel()` sets `cancelAtPeriodEnd: true`; tenant stays ACTIVE until `applyScheduledCancellations` runs at period end). Before that date they visit /choose-plan to compare, decide to "downgrade instead of leaving" is not what they want, or simply click the cheaper plan to see the price and then commit. The button reads "Schedule downgrade", the preview shows no warning, and the success toast says "Downgrade scheduled — You'll move to the Starter plan at the end of your current cycle" — none of which says the cancellation is now void. `downgrade()` sets `cancelAtPeriodEnd: false`, `applyScheduledCancellations` will never fire, and the tenant is billed on the cheaper plan indefinitely believing they had cancelled. The identical silent revocation happens on the UPGRADE branch.

The code already has the warning mechanism and the state in hand — it is applied to one branch of four.
findings.fixHint: In planChangePreview, attach a warning to the UPGRADE and DOWNGRADE branches too when `priorSub.cancelAtPeriodEnd` (or a differing `downgradeToPlanKey`) is armed, e.g. "Your scheduled cancellation will be cancelled" — and consider gating the commit behind the same acknowledgement checkbox the seat warning uses.
findings.decision: KEEP_CURRENT warns that committing cancels a pending change but the UPGRADE and DOWNGRADE branches, which both set cancelAtPeriodEnd:false on commit, say nothing; the state is identical and the warning belongs on all three. Real inconsistency at the point of decision, but the commit outcome (keep the subscription) is the plausible intent, so minor.

findings.summary: A published plan key outside PLAN_KEYS ranks -1, so the preview classifies it as a DOWNGRADE from every plan, downgrade() accepts it, and the cron then writes basePriceSnapshot: null — where the old subscribe() route priced it correctly.
findings.detail:
`planRank` (plan-catalog.constants.ts:101-104) returns -1 for any key `normalizePlanKey` cannot resolve (not in `PLAN_KEYS = [STARTER, GROWTH, SCALE, ENTERPRISE]` and not in `LEGACY_PLAN_KEY_ALIASES = {TEAM, BUSINESS, PROFESSIONAL}`). The published catalog is DATA (a PlanVersion published by `db:publish:catalog:v11`); I found no code path that constrains a published `PlanDefinition.planKey` to PLAN_KEYS.

So the day a catalog version publishes a plan key that was not also added to PLAN_KEYS (say 'PRO'), the chooser lists it (usePlans -> /billing/plans) and:
- planChangePreview line 427-433: `rankTo = -1 < rankFrom` for every existing plan -> DOWNGRADE, unconditionally.
- downgrade() line 593: `planRank('PRO') >= planRank(from)` is `-1 >= 0..3` = false -> accepted; `def` IS found in the published catalog so the earlier check passes. The schedule is written.
- billing-cron applyScheduledDowngrades line 149-158: `findPlanDefinition(pinnedVersion, 'PRO')` normalizes to 'PRO' and finds nothing in an older pinned version -> `targetDef === undefined` -> `basePriceSnapshot: null` and `amountDelta = 0 - oldMonthly`; `planKeyToEnum('PRO')` (constants:199-210) falls through to 'STARTER' for `currentPlan` and `Tenant.plan`. The tenant lands on a plan with a NULL base price — `MrrService` prices from the snapshot, so they are free.

Before this diff the same pick went through subscribe(), which reads `def` from the PUBLISHED catalog and writes `basePriceSnapshot: def.monthlyPrice` — the correct price. The new B58 guard (line 187, `planRank(input.planKey) !== planRank(fromKey)`) additionally now 409s that path for an ACTIVE tenant, so the correct route is closed and only the broken one is open. Reachability depends on an operational mistake (publishing an off-list key), which is why I am scoring this minor rather than major.
findings.fixHint: Reject an unrankable key explicitly rather than letting -1 mean "lowest": in planChangePreview return SUBSCRIBE (or throw) when `planRank(planKey) < 0`, and in downgrade() refuse when either rank is -1. A catalog-publish-time assertion that every definition's planKey normalizes into PLAN_KEYS would close it at the source.
findings.decision: planRank returns -1 for an unknown key and neither planChangePreview nor downgrade() rejects a negative rank, so a published key outside PLAN_KEYS is classified DOWNGRADE from every plan and the cron writes basePriceSnapshot null where subscribe() used to price it. Contingent on a future catalog publish, but a negative-rank guard is the cheap correct fix and the evidence is not refuted; kept as minor.

confirmedFindings.summary: Routing plan changes to upgrade()/downgrade() leaves the scheduled-transition fields (downgradeToPlanKey/downgradeEffectiveAt, cancelAtPeriodEnd) armed, which the old subscribe() path always cleared.
confirmedFindings.detail: subscribe()'s update block (lines 216-218) clears `cancelAtPeriodEnd:false, downgradeToPlanKey:null, downgradeEffectiveAt:null` on every commit. upgrade()'s updateMany (lines 399-407) writes ONLY planKey/currentPlan/planVersionId/basePriceSnapshot, and downgrade() (447-449) writes only the downgrade fields — neither clears the other's markers. Before this change /choose-plan always went through subscribe(), so every commit disarmed a pending schedule. Concrete failure: ACTIVE tenant on GROWTH MONTHLY opens /choose-plan and picks STARTER -> planChangePreview returns DOWNGRADE -> dispatchPlanChange fires POST /billing/subscription/downgrade -> downgradeToPlanKey='STARTER', downgradeEffectiveAt=periodEnd. The tenant changes their mind and picks SCALE -> preview returns UPGRADE (rank 2 > 1) -> upgrade() sets planKey='SCALE' and the toast says "Upgraded — You're now on the Scale plan" — but downgradeToPlanKey/downgradeEffectiveAt are untouched. At period end billing-cron.service.ts:122 applyScheduledDowngrades selects purely on `downgradeEffectiveAt lte now && downgradeToPlanKey not null` (no rank/current-plan check) and silently drops the tenant from SCALE to STARTER, re-pricing basePriceSnapshot and — if the team is over STARTER's seat cap — deactivating users. Second scenario, same root: a tenant with cancelAtPeriodEnd=true (settings/billing "Cancel") who then upgrades from /choose-plan keeps the cancellation and goes READ_ONLY at period end (billing-cron applyScheduledCancellations) despite the "Upgraded" toast; previously the subscribe() call cleared it. Lesson L-046 covers exactly this shape ("undo a claim only by compare-and-set on the value the claim wrote" / a write and its record share one condition).
confirmedFindings.fixHint: upgrade() (and downgrade(), for cancelAtPeriodEnd) must clear the sibling scheduled-transition fields inside the same transaction that changes the plan — i.e. enumerate every field subscribe()'s update block wrote — or planChangePreview must refuse/route differently while a schedule is armed.

confirmedFindings.summary: NOOP for same plan+cycle removes the only self-service way to cancel a scheduled downgrade, which was previously done by re-picking the current plan on /choose-plan.
confirmedFindings.detail: planChangePreview returns `{action:'NOOP'}` whenever `priorSub.planKey === planKey && priorSub.cycle === cycle`, ignoring downgradeToPlanKey/cancelAtPeriodEnd. choose-plan/page.tsx:234 then disables the commit button (`disabled={isCommitting || changeAction === "NOOP"}`, label "Current plan") and commit() early-returns at page.tsx:73. Before this change, an ACTIVE tenant with a pending downgrade could open /choose-plan, re-pick their current plan and click "Subscribe to X"; subscribe()'s update (lines 216-218) cleared downgradeToPlanKey/downgradeEffectiveAt/cancelAtPeriodEnd. There is no other undo: apps/web/app/(dashboard)/settings/billing/page.tsx:176-183 only *displays* "Scheduled to change to X on <date>" with no control, and useResumeSubscription/POST /billing/subscription/resume only clears cancelAtPeriodEnd (subscription-mutation.service.ts:489). Grep confirms downgradeToPlanKey is written in exactly three places: subscribe() (clears), downgrade() (sets), billing-cron applyScheduledDowngrades (clears on apply). Concrete failure: tenant schedules a downgrade by mis-clicking the new one-click "Schedule downgrade", returns to /choose-plan, picks their current plan, and finds a disabled "Current plan" button — the downgrade fires at period end with no way for the tenant to stop it.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Either surface the armed schedule in the preview (e.g. a CANCEL_SCHEDULED action / non-NOOP when downgradeToPlanKey or cancelAtPeriodEnd is set) so the current-plan pick clears it, or add an explicit "Keep my plan" control for a scheduled downgrade in settings/billing backed by an endpoint that clears the two fields.

confirmedFindings.summary: dispatchPlanChange hard-codes retainedUserIds: [] on every downgrade, which deactivates EVERY operator and driver at period end when the team is over the new seat cap.
confirmedFindings.detail: `mutations.downgrade({ targetPlanKey: preview.planKey, retainedUserIds: [] }, options)` is now the first and only web caller of POST /billing/subscription/downgrade (grep: useDowngrade had zero callers before this change). The empty list flows through settings-billing.controller.ts:129 -> downgrade() line 449 -> billing-cron.service.ts:186, where the seat sweep is `updateMany({ where: { role in [OPERATOR, DRIVER], status:'ACTIVE', deletedAt:null, id: { notIn: s.retainedUserIds } }, data:{ status:'INACTIVE' } })`. `notIn: []` matches every row — the existing pin billing-cron.service.spec.ts:189-205 states this outright ("notIn [] matches all -> deactivates every non-admin operator/driver", asserting `where.id` equals `{ notIn: [] }`). Concrete failure: an ACTIVE tenant on SCALE with 12 operators/drivers clicks "Schedule downgrade" for GROWTH (5 seats) on /choose-plan; the Summary shows only "$0" and "Takes effect <date>" — no seat warning anywhere in the card (choose-plan/page.tsx:203-229). At period end activeTeam(12) > seatCap(5) so all 12 operators and drivers are set INACTIVE, leaving only TENANT_ADMINs able to sign in. The build plan lists a seat picker as a non-goal, but it does not cover shipping a one-click, unwarned entrance to the full wipe.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: At minimum surface the consequence in the DOWNGRADE summary (seats included vs. active team, "all other users will be deactivated") before the commit; better, pass the current active OPERATOR/DRIVER ids up to the target cap as retainedUserIds instead of [].

confirmedFindings.summary: The B73 FOR UPDATE lock is inert on the hook paths that reach runSync with a non-transactional client, so the duplicate-CLAWBACK race stays open there.
confirmedFindings.detail: The docblock's contract ("runSync must always be called with a transactional client") is false for shipped call paths. orders.service.ts:2650 (manual mark-DELIVERED), 4277 and 5251 (post-commit order edit) call `invoicesService.reconcileOrderDraftInvoice(id, { basis: 'order' })` with no `tx`; invoices.service.ts:1293 then resolves `const db = opts.tx ?? this.prisma.forTenant()` — a plain extended client, not a transaction — and that same `db` is threaded to `syncInvoiceCommissionSafe` at invoices.service.ts:1433 (deposit-mirror branch) and, via reconcileSplitOrderDrafts -> rebuildSiblingDrafts (invoices.service.ts:2103 -> 1855), to the sibling rebuild path. runSync then issues `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` in its own implicit single-statement transaction: the row lock is released before `db.invoice.findUnique` and before the CommissionAdjustment insert, so two such callers (or one such caller interleaving with a transactional writer between its lock release and its read) both read zero prior adjustments and both append the same CLAWBACK — the exact B73 failure. The cron path (commission-reconciliation.service.ts:58, no db -> tenantTransaction) and the tx-passing hook sites are genuinely fixed; these three are not, and the class docblock at lines 36-41 asserts the "exactly one" invariant without that qualification.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Either make runSync open its own tenantTransaction when `db` is not transactional (detect and wrap), or fix the callers so reconcileOrderDraftInvoice runs inside a tenantTransaction like resyncOrderInvoicesForEdit already does; if neither, the residual must be filed and the class docblock's unqualified 'exactly one' claim corrected.

confirmedFindings.summary: The upgrade hit counter also counts the GET /billing/subscription the post-success redirect triggers, so the assertions can flake.
confirmedFindings.detail: mockMutations' third route matches any request to `/billing/subscription` regardless of method. On success, dispatchPlanChange's onSuccess (choose-plan/page.tsx:96) sets `window.location.href = '/settings/billing'`, and that page's useSubscription (apps/web/lib/api/billing.ts:149-153) issues GET /billing/subscription — which the page-level route interception still serves after navigation, incrementing hits.upgrade. In the DOWNGRADE test the assertion `expect(hits.upgrade).toBe(0)` (line 240) then fails whenever the redirect completes before the preceding `expect.poll(() => hits.downgrade).toBe(1)` resolves (poll retries at 100/250/500/1000ms, so a slow first POST on a loaded runner leaves ample time for the redirect's GET). In the UPGRADE tests, if the GET lands before the poll's first passing check, hits.upgrade is already 2 and `expect.poll(...).toBe(1)` can never pass. Not observed running (Playwright was not executed here), but the counting path is unconditional.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Count only POSTs in the three mutation route handlers (`if (route.request().method() === 'POST')`), or snapshot the counters before the redirect completes.

confirmedFindings.summary: The B58 guard and planChangePreview both key on priorSub.planKey alone, so an ACTIVE tenant whose subscription predates plans-as-data (planKey NULL, legacy tenant.plan enum) still reaches the exact bug the fix exists to close.
confirmedFindings.detail: TenantSubscription.planKey is nullable (apps/api/prisma/schema/platform.prisma:46 — added later, 'all nullable/defaulted so existing rows are untouched') and four production sites treat NULL planKey on a live tenant as a normal state by falling back to the legacy enum: entitlements.service.ts:144, platform-pricing.service.ts:85, platform-admin.service.ts:702 and :1220. Neither new code path does that fallback. Scenario: tenant status ACTIVE, subscription {planKey: null, currentPlan: BUSINESS, cycle: MONTHLY, periodStart/periodEnd mid-cycle}; a TENANT_ADMIN opens /choose-plan and picks STARTER. planChangePreview (line 326: `if (tenant?.status !== "ACTIVE" || !priorSub?.planKey)`) returns action SUBSCRIBE, so the chooser renders 'Subscribe to Starter' and posts /billing/subscribe; the guard at line 148 (`priorSub?.planKey &&`) is falsy and does not fire; subscribe() upserts with periodStart = now / periodEnd = now+1mo. That is B58's whole harm reproduced — instant downgrade, MeterUsage re-bucketed onto a new periodStart, renewal date jumped — plus the PLAN_CHANGED amountDelta is computed from planMonthly(version, null) = 0 (line 192), so MRR is booked as a full positive base instead of the signed change. The ruling's §2 wording ('priorSub?.planKey') is a hypothesis about which states reach the bad path; re-derivation shows it leaves this one open.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Resolve the prior plan the way the rest of the codebase does before ranking: select `plan` alongside `status` on the tenant read and use `normalizePlanKey(priorSub?.planKey) ?? planKeyFromEnum(tenant.plan)` as the 'from' key in BOTH subscribe()'s guard and planChangePreview()'s early return, so a legacy row is classified UPGRADE/DOWNGRADE instead of SUBSCRIBE. Add a T1/T2 case with `sub: { planKey: null, cycle: 'MONTHLY' }` + tenant `{status:'ACTIVE', plan:'BUSINESS'}`.

confirmedFindings.summary: dispatchPlanChange schedules downgrades with retainedUserIds: [], which the period-end cron reads as 'keep only admins' — the chooser can now silently deactivate every operator and driver in the tenant with no warning at the point of decision.
confirmedFindings.detail: billing-cron.service.ts applyScheduledDowngrades reads the stored retainedUserIds (line 131), and when the team is over the target plan's seatCap it runs `user.updateMany({ role: { in: ['OPERATOR','DRIVER'] }, status: 'ACTIVE', id: { notIn: s.retainedUserIds } }, { status: 'INACTIVE' })` (lines 179-188) — its own comment says 'An empty retained list = keep only admins.' Before this change `useDowngrade` had ZERO callers in apps/web (grep of apps/web/app: only choose-plan/page.tsx references it), so POST /billing/subscription/downgrade was reachable only by a direct API call. Scenario: tenant ACTIVE on GROWTH (seatsIncluded 10) with 8 active OPERATOR/DRIVER users; TENANT_ADMIN opens /choose-plan, picks STARTER (seatsIncluded 3). The quote returns DOWNGRADE, the summary shows only 'Due today $0' and 'Takes effect <periodEnd>', the button reads 'Schedule downgrade'; one click stores retainedUserIds = []. At period end the cron deactivates all 8 operators/drivers (not just the 5 over cap) — every non-admin user in the tenant loses access, with nothing in the UI having said so. The ruling makes a seat picker a non-goal, but nothing in it required the seat consequence to be invisible: PlanChangePreview already carries a `warning` field that choose-plan renders (page.tsx:227-229) and that is used for the cycle-switch case only.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Either populate the warning server-side for DOWNGRADE when active OPERATOR/DRIVER count exceeds the target plan's seatsIncluded ('N users will be deactivated on <effectiveAt>') and render it as a confirm step, or have the API default retainedUserIds to the first seatCap active users rather than [] when the caller sends an empty list. Decide which before shipping the web half; the current pairing is the destructive combination.

confirmedFindings.summary: The mutation hit counters are method-agnostic, so the settings/billing page's GET /billing/subscription after the success redirect is counted as an upgrade hit and can break the T4 assertions.
confirmedFindings.detail: mockMutations registers `page.route(/\/billing\/subscription(\?.*)?$/)` and increments hits.upgrade for ANY method. On success, choose-plan's commit() sets `window.location.href = '/settings/billing'` (page.tsx:96); that page calls useSubscription() (settings/billing/page.tsx:84), which issues GET /billing/subscription — the only other caller of that path in apps/web. Test 1 asserts `expect.poll(() => hits.upgrade).toBe(1)`: once the redirect lands, the counter becomes 2 and can never return to 1, so a slow poll tick turns into a hard timeout failure rather than a flake that self-heals. Test 2 is worse-shaped: after `expect.poll(() => hits.downgrade).toBe(1)` it asserts `expect(hits.upgrade).toBe(0)` (line 240), which fails outright if the redirect's GET has landed by then. Both are timing-dependent, and this spec runs post-deploy where a red is expensive to diagnose.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Count only the mutation: in each handler, `if (route.request().method() !== 'POST') return route.continue()` (or fulfil without incrementing) before bumping the counter.

confirmedFindings.summary: The spec header justifies having no local test for the web dispatch logic with a false claim that apps/web has no unit runner, leaving dispatchPlanChange and the NOOP-disable criterion with no gate that runs before deploy.
confirmedFindings.detail: The header states the spec is out of the local red gate because 'apps/web has no unit runner for its client-side routing logic'. apps/web does have Jest + RTL: `npx jest --silent` in apps/web ran 30 suites / 161 tests in this session, including pure-lib specs (lib/calendar-date.test.ts) and full component specs (app/(auth)/login/page.test.tsx, settings-users.test.tsx). dispatchPlanChange is an exported pure function in lib/api/billing.ts taking a QuoteResult and three plain callbacks — nothing about it needs a browser. As things stand, ruling §2's web acceptance criteria (dispatch on change.action, NOOP disabled, per-action labels) are proven only by the change-plan-routing Playwright project, which runs post-deploy; a regression in the routing branch reaches production before any gate sees it, and the 'NOOP disabled' criterion has no test in any layer (T4 has no NOOP case).
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Add apps/web/lib/api/billing.test.ts exercising dispatchPlanChange for the four actions (UPGRADE → upgrade({planKey}), DOWNGRADE → downgrade({targetPlanKey, retainedUserIds: []}), SUBSCRIBE and change:null → subscribe({planKey, cycle}), NOOP → no mutation called), and correct the header's rationale.

confirmedFindings.summary: isStripeResourceMissing's docblock states the opposite of the policy the function implements — it says any Stripe error means the resource is already gone.
confirmedFindings.detail: The comment reads 'A Stripe error means the resource we tried to act on is already gone (deleted subscription item, e.g.) — safe to treat as a no-op success rather than a failure to surface to the caller.' The function actually returns true only for `code === 'resource_missing'` or `statusCode === 404`, and the entire B107 fix depends on every OTHER error class being surfaced as a 503 refusal (disableAddon lines 217-231). A maintainer reading this docblock in a money/entitlement path is told the swallow-everything behaviour the change was written to remove; the next person widening the predicate 'to match the comment' re-opens B107.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Reword to name the class, e.g. 'A Stripe resource_missing / 404 error means the item we tried to act on is already gone — treat that ONE case as a no-op success; every other Stripe failure must be surfaced to the caller.'

confirmedFindings.summary: Every new B107 test covers a refusal path; the Stripe-configured SUCCESS paths that the fix rewrote are covered by no test at all.
confirmedFindings.detail: make() defaults to `{ isConfigured: false, client: {} }`, and the only tests that inject a configured client are T7 (del rejects api_error), T11 (del rejects resource_missing), T8 (create rejects), T9 (no stripeSubId, create never called) and T12 (no price, Stripe untouched). No test in the repo ever resolves `subscriptionItems.create` or `subscriptionItems.del`. Failure scenario: change `stripeItemId = item.id` to `stripeItemId = null` at apps/api/src/billing/addon.service.ts:157 (or make the success branch throw) and the whole suite still passes — I ran `npx jest src/billing src/sales-agents` equivalents for these four files and got 57/57 green, with zero of those 57 exercising a successful Stripe write. The paid-add-on happy path (upsert must persist the real Stripe item id, entitlements must be invalidated) is the main path the P1 diff restructured and it has no oracle.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Add two cases to addon.service.spec.ts: (a) enableAddon('t1','msrp','price_1') with `subscription:{stripeSubId:'sub_1'}` and `create` resolving `{id:'si_9'}` -> assert tenantAddon.upsert called with stripeItemId 'si_9' and entitlements.invalidate('t1'); (b) disableAddon with `del` resolving -> assert update `{active:false, stripeItemId:null}` and that del was called with the item id.

confirmedFindings.summary: The T2 UPGRADE test asserts only `proratedNow > 0`, so the money figure the chooser renders as "Due today" has no value oracle anywhere in the suite.
confirmedFindings.detail: T2's UPGRADE case (`expect(preview?.proratedNow ?? 0).toBeGreaterThan(0)`) is the only assertion on the prorated charge. With the fixture (TEAM 149 -> BUSINESS 349, period now-15d..now+15d) the correct value is ~100.00; an implementation that returned the un-prorated monthly delta (200), the full new plan price (349), or the full new price prorated (~174.50) all pass this test. No existing test pins `proratedDiff`/`upgrade()`'s prorated amount either (the upgrade tests at :227-262 assert only the MRR delta 290 and the updateMany guard), so nothing in the API suite constrains the number. apps/web/app/(dashboard)/choose-plan/page.tsx now prefers `preview.change?.proratedNow` over `dueToday` for the "Due today" line, so a wrong value is charged/shown with the whole suite green.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Assert the value, e.g. `expect(preview.proratedNow).toBeCloseTo(100, 1)` for the 15/30-day fixture (the period is an exact 30 days, so the figure is deterministic to the cent-ish), and add one lower-bound/upper-bound sanity assertion that it is strictly less than the full monthly delta.

confirmedFindings.summary: The `upgrade` hit counter matches any HTTP method on /billing/subscription, and the page the successful commit redirects to issues a GET on exactly that URL.
confirmedFindings.detail: mockMutations counts every request matching /\/billing\/subscription(\?.*)?$/ as an upgrade, without checking `route.request().method()`. commit()'s onSuccess does `window.location.href = "/settings/billing"` (apps/web/app/(dashboard)/choose-plan/page.tsx), and apps/web/app/(dashboard)/settings/billing/page.tsx:84 calls useSubscription(), which GETs `/billing/subscription` (apps/web/lib/api/billing.ts:152). Failure scenario: DOWNGRADE test — `await expect.poll(() => hits.downgrade).toBe(1)` resolves, the redirect fires, the settings page's GET is counted, and the very next line `expect(hits.upgrade).toBe(0)` (line 240) reads 1 -> red for a correct implementation. UPGRADE test — `expect.poll(() => hits.upgrade).toBe(1)` (line 210) can observe 2 after the redirect's GET lands and then never returns to 1 -> red. The same conflation also weakens the oracle: a plain GET would satisfy "the upgrade endpoint was hit".
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Count only POSTs in each handler (`if (route.request().method() === "POST") hits.x += 1;`), and/or assert the counters before allowing the post-success navigation.

confirmedFindings.summary: The catalogV8() "RANK BASIS" docblock documents an oracle (monthlyPrice inside the published catalog) that the implementation does not use (planRank's PLAN_KEYS index + alias table).
confirmedFindings.detail: The spec comment at :41-46 states rank is a plan's `monthlyPrice` within the same published catalog, and the fixture gains retained TEAM 249 / BUSINESS 499 definitions at :57-59 to support that claim. planChangePreview (apps/api/src/billing/subscription-mutation.service.ts:348-349) and the subscribe() guard both rank with `planRank()`, which is `PLAN_KEYS.indexOf(normalizePlanKey(...))` — a hardcoded ordering plus LEGACY_PLAN_KEY_ALIASES, i.e. exactly the "alias table" the test plan said should not be relied on. The two oracles agree only because the fixture's prices were chosen to match the alias ranks, so no test distinguishes them: a published catalog whose prices contradict PLAN_KEYS order (e.g. a repriced GROWTH above SCALE) would classify an upgrade as a downgrade with every test still green, and the added legacy definitions are inert for the assertions actually made.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Either state the real oracle in the comment (planRank/PLAN_KEYS + LEGACY_PLAN_KEY_ALIASES) or add a case whose catalog prices disagree with PLAN_KEYS order and pin which one wins.

confirmedFindings.summary: The DOWNGRADE test's only oracle is a hit count — it never asserts the request body, so the destructive `retainedUserIds: []` payload the chooser now sends is unverified.
confirmedFindings.detail: The route handler fulfils 200 without inspecting the request, so nothing checks what dispatchPlanChange posts. apps/web/lib/api/billing.ts:275 sends `{ targetPlanKey, retainedUserIds: [] }`; apps/api/src/billing/billing-cron.service.ts:168-186 documents "An empty retained list = keep only admins" and deactivates every non-retained ACTIVE OPERATOR/DRIVER once the tenant is over the new seat cap. The chooser is the first web caller of the downgrade endpoint, and a test suite that asserts only "the downgrade URL was hit" cannot distinguish a safe payload from one that deactivates the whole non-admin team at period end. (The server default is also `[]` — apps/api/src/billing/settings-billing.controller.ts:129 — so this is not a client/server divergence, but it is an unasserted consequence introduced into this flow.)
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Capture `route.request().postDataJSON()` in the downgrade handler and assert the body (targetPlanKey, and whatever the intended retained-seats contract is); if `[]` is intended, add a comment/assert making that explicit.

confirmedFindings.summary: The new DOWNGRADE dispatch always posts `retainedUserIds: []`, and the period-end cron reads an empty retained list as "deactivate every OPERATOR and DRIVER".
confirmedFindings.detail: `dispatchPlanChange` (apps/web/lib/api/billing.ts:275) fires `mutations.downgrade({ targetPlanKey, retainedUserIds: [] })`. Before this change `useDowngrade` was defined but called from NO UI (grep over apps/web: the only pre-existing references were the hook definition and the read-only "Scheduled to change to …" banner in settings/billing/page.tsx), so `/choose-plan` is the first user-reachable path to POST /billing/subscription/downgrade. `downgrade()` persists that array verbatim (apps/api/src/billing/subscription-mutation.service.ts:449), and `billing-cron.service.ts:171-190` then does: if the tenant's active TENANT_ADMIN+OPERATOR+DRIVER count exceeds the target plan's `seatsIncluded`, `user.updateMany({ role: { in: ['OPERATOR','DRIVER'] }, status: 'ACTIVE', id: { notIn: s.retainedUserIds } }, { status: 'INACTIVE' })` — with an empty array Prisma's `notIn: []` matches every row (the code's own comment says "An empty retained list = keep only admins"). Concrete scenario: a tenant on GROWTH (10 seats) with 6 operators and 2 drivers picks STARTER (3 seats) on /choose-plan; the chooser shows only "Downgrade scheduled — You'll move to the Starter plan at the end of your current cycle" (choose-plan/page.tsx:79-82) with no mention of seats; at period end all 6 operators and both drivers are set INACTIVE and can no longer log in. Over-cap is the normal case for a downgrade, not an edge case. The build plan lists "a seat picker for downgrades" as a non-goal, but it does not sanction shipping a silent mass-deactivation trigger behind an unlabelled button.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Either send the tenant's current active OPERATOR/DRIVER ids as `retainedUserIds` (preserving today's seat state), or block the DOWNGRADE dispatch behind an explicit confirmation that names how many staff accounts will be deactivated at period end. Do not leave `[]` as the silent default on a user-facing control.

confirmedFindings.summary: The B73 `FOR UPDATE` lock does not span the read-then-append critical section on a live call path that passes a non-transactional client, and the docblock asserts a contract that path violates.
confirmedFindings.detail: `runSync` opens with `await db.$executeRaw\`SELECT id FROM \"CommissionAccrual\" WHERE \"invoiceId\" = ${invoiceId} FOR UPDATE\`` and its docblock states the contract "`runSync` must always be called with a transactional client … a non-transactional `db` makes it a no-op", filing only `removeInvoiceCommission` as the residual. A live caller breaks that contract today: apps/api/src/orders/orders.service.ts:2650 (manual mark-DELIVERED) and :4277 (order-item edit, non-partial-billing branch) call `this.invoicesService.reconcileOrderDraftInvoice(id, { basis: 'order' })` with NO tx; apps/api/src/invoices/invoices.service.ts:1293 resolves `const db = opts.tx ?? this.prisma.forTenant()` — an autocommit `$extends` client — and line 1433 passes that same `db` into `syncInvoiceCommissionSafe(draft.id, db)` for the issued deposit-mirror branch. `syncInvoiceCommission` sees a truthy `db` and calls `runSync(invoiceId, db)` directly (commission-engine.service.ts:63-64), so the SELECT … FOR UPDATE commits and releases the row lock before the invoice read at line 208 and before the adjustment insert. Failure scenario: two staff save edits on the same delivered order with a deposit-mirror invoice within the same second (or one such edit overlaps the :30 reconciliation window after the cron has committed); both statements take and immediately release the accrual lock, both then read `adjustments: []` for an accrual whose claimedAmount exceeds payable, and both append a CLAWBACK — the exact duplicate-adjustment outcome B73 exists to prevent. `syncInvoiceCommissionSafe` swallows any error, so nothing surfaces. This also mirrors lesson L-081: a guard placed at one call site's client is bypassed by sibling doors.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Either make the lock unconditional by opening a transaction inside `runSync` when `db` is not transactional, or fix the two callers (`orders.service.ts:2650` / `:4277`) to hand `reconcileOrderDraftInvoice` a `tenantTransaction` tx. At minimum the docblock must stop claiming the contract holds and must name this path as an open residual.

confirmedFindings.summary: For an ACTIVE subscription with a null `periodEnd`, the new preview reports DOWNGRADE and the resulting schedule can never be applied by the cron — the UI reports success and the tenant keeps paying the old rate.
confirmedFindings.detail: `planChangePreview`'s DOWNGRADE branch returns `effectiveAt: priorSub.periodEnd`, and `periodEnd` is nullable (`apps/api/prisma/schema/platform.prisma:41`). An ACTIVE tenant can hold a subscription row with a null period: `platform-admin.service.ts:437-451` upserts TenantSubscription with `currentPlan`/`planKey`/`planVersionId`/`basePriceSnapshot` only — it never writes `periodStart`/`periodEnd` — so any tenant whose plan was set by a platform admin without ever going through `subscribe()` is in that state. Scenario: such a tenant opens /choose-plan and picks a lower plan. `planChangePreview` returns `{action:'DOWNGRADE', effectiveAt:null}`; choose-plan/page.tsx:218 falls through the `preview.change?.effectiveAt` truthiness test and shows "Renews <fresh quote date>" instead of an effective date; the button reads "Schedule downgrade"; on click `downgrade()` writes `downgradeEffectiveAt: sub.periodEnd` = null (subscription-mutation.service.ts:448) and the client toasts "Downgrade scheduled". `billing-cron.service.ts:125` selects only `downgradeEffectiveAt: { not: null, lte: now }`, so the row is never picked up: the downgrade never applies, /settings/billing shows a scheduled change with a blank date forever, and the tenant keeps being billed the higher plan. Before this change `downgrade()` had no UI caller, so this was unreachable.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Have `planChangePreview` refuse to classify DOWNGRADE (or return an explicit warning/blocking state) when `priorSub.periodEnd` is null, and/or make `downgrade()` reject a subscription with no `periodEnd` rather than persisting an unappliable schedule.

confirmedFindings.summary: The `upgrade` mock route also matches the GET /billing/subscription the post-commit redirect issues, so `hits.upgrade` can be incremented by a read and turn the assertions false-red.
confirmedFindings.detail: `mockMutations` registers `page.route(/\/billing\/subscription(\?.*)?$/)` without filtering on request method, and it increments `hits.upgrade` for every match. After a successful commit, choose-plan/page.tsx:96 does `window.location.href = "/settings/billing"`, and that page calls `useSubscription()` → `apiClient.get("/billing/subscription")` (apps/web/lib/api/billing.ts:152), which matches the same pattern. In the DOWNGRADE test the trailing synchronous `expect(hits.upgrade).toBe(0)` (line 240) is evaluated after `expect.poll(() => hits.downgrade).toBe(1)` resolves; if the redirect's GET lands inside that window on a slow deployed environment the counter reads 1 and the regression test fails for a reason unrelated to the behaviour under test. The same collision can push `hits.upgrade` past 1 in the two UPGRADE tests.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Filter the handler on method — e.g. `if (route.request().method() !== "POST") return route.continue();` before incrementing — in all three mutation routes.

confirmedFindings.summary: The new self-service DOWNGRADE dispatch sends `retainedUserIds: []`, which the period-end cron reads as "deactivate every operator and driver", and nothing in the preview or the UI warns the tenant.
confirmedFindings.detail: `dispatchPlanChange` posts `{targetPlanKey, retainedUserIds: []}`. `downgrade()` stores that list verbatim (subscription-mutation.service.ts:449) and `billing-cron.service.ts:168-186` (`applyScheduledDowngrades`, @LeaderCron "0 2 * * *") does: if `activeTeam > seatCap`, `user.updateMany({ role: {in:[OPERATOR,DRIVER]}, status: ACTIVE, id: { notIn: s.retainedUserIds } }, { status: INACTIVE })` — its own comment says "An empty retained list = keep only admins". Grep shows `useDowngrade` had NO UI caller before this diff (only apps/web/lib/api/billing.ts declared it), so this change makes the path reachable for the first time. Scenario: an ACTIVE tenant on a 10-seat plan with 6 operators/drivers opens /choose-plan (reachable from settings/billing's "Change plan" button), picks the 3-seat STARTER, sees only "Downgrade scheduled — You'll move to the Starter plan at the end of your current cycle", and 30 days later at 02:00 UTC all 6 operators/drivers are set INACTIVE and cannot log in. The `PlanChangePreview.warning` field exists and is populated only for a cycle switch; the DOWNGRADE branch (subscription-mutation.service.ts:369-375) has every input needed (targetDef.seatsIncluded vs. the active team count) and emits no warning. A seat picker is an explicit non-goal in the build plan, but the silent mass deactivation is not addressed by anything in the diff.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: In `planChangePreview`'s DOWNGRADE branch, count ACTIVE TENANT_ADMIN/OPERATOR/DRIVER users against the target definition's `seatsIncluded` and set `warning` (e.g. "N users will be deactivated at period end"); render it (choose-plan already prints `preview.change.warning`) and require an explicit confirm before dispatching the downgrade.

confirmedFindings.summary: Once a downgrade is scheduled there is no way to cancel it: `subscribe()` was the only writer that cleared `downgradeToPlanKey`, and the new NOOP branch plus the new ACTIVE guard both close that door — while `upgrade()` leaves the pending downgrade to fire later.
confirmedFindings.detail: Grep for writers of `downgradeToPlanKey`/`downgradeEffectiveAt` returns exactly three: `subscribe()`'s upsert clears them (subscription-mutation.service.ts:217-218), `downgrade()` sets them (:447-448), and the cron clears them when it applies (billing-cron.service.ts:159-160). `resume()` (:483-493) only clears `cancelAtPeriodEnd`, and settings/billing/page.tsx:176-181 only DISPLAYS the pending change — there is no cancel control. Before this diff an ACTIVE tenant could clear a pending downgrade by re-picking their current plan on /choose-plan (that call reached `subscribe()`). After it: re-picking the current plan returns NOOP (:334) and the commit button is disabled with label "Current plan" (choose-plan/page.tsx:214-224), and picking any other same-cycle plan of a different rank now 409s at the new guard (:148-155). Worse, picking a HIGHER plan routes to `upgrade()`, which updates planKey/currentPlan/planVersionId/basePriceSnapshot and never touches the downgrade fields — so the tenant pays `proratedNow` immediately and at period end `applyScheduledDowngrades` (whose filter is only `downgradeEffectiveAt != null && <= now`) still applies the stale `downgradeToPlanKey`, dropping them back to the lower plan and triggering the seat deactivation above.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Clear `downgradeToPlanKey`/`downgradeEffectiveAt` inside `upgrade()`'s transaction, and give the tenant an explicit undo — either a cancel-downgrade mutation surfaced on settings/billing, or let NOOP-with-a-pending-downgrade render an enabled "Keep my current plan" action instead of a disabled button.

confirmedFindings.summary: For an ACTIVE tenant whose subscription has a null `periodEnd`, the chooser promises a scheduled downgrade that the cron can never apply, and the new guard removes the only path that used to heal the null period.
confirmedFindings.detail: `periodEnd` is nullable (platform.prisma:41). `planChangePreview` returns `action: "DOWNGRADE", effectiveAt: priorSub.periodEnd` with no null check (:369-375); `downgrade()` then writes `downgradeEffectiveAt: sub.periodEnd` = null (:448); `applyScheduledDowngrades` selects `where: { downgradeEffectiveAt: { not: null, lte: now } }` (billing-cron.service.ts:125), so the row is never picked up, and `rollCycles` skips it too (`periodEnd: { not: null, lt: now }`, :279). The user sees the toast "Downgrade scheduled — at the end of your current cycle" and settings/billing shows a pending change with a blank date, forever; the summary card even renders "Renews …" instead of "Takes effect …" because the DOWNGRADE branch of choose-plan/page.tsx:212 requires a non-null `effectiveAt`. Such rows are producible today: `platform-admin.service.ts:436-451` (`changePlan`) upserts TenantSubscription with `planKey` set and no `periodStart`/`periodEnd` in either the create or update block, on a tenant that `updateStatus` (:361-365) flipped to ACTIVE. Before this diff those tenants went through `subscribe()`, which sets `periodStart`/`periodEnd` and healed the null; the new 409 guard (:148-155) plus the NOOP branch now make `subscribe()` unreachable for them. I could not query production to count how many rows are in this state.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Treat a null `periodEnd` explicitly: either return SUBSCRIBE (or DOWNGRADE with a warning) from `planChangePreview` when `priorSub.periodEnd == null`, or have `downgrade()` refuse / fall back to a computed period end rather than writing a `downgradeEffectiveAt` the cron filters out.

confirmedFindings.summary: The new 409 refusal on the money path leaves no server-side trace, and the web toast discards the actionable message it carries.
confirmedFindings.detail: This repo already documents that a handled 4xx is invisible: addon.guard.ts:88-90 — "SentryExceptionFilter captures >= 500 only, and there is no access-log middleware" (confirmed in common/sentry-exception.filter.ts, which only captures status >= 500) — and logs its denials for exactly that reason. The new `ConflictException` in `subscribe()` (:148-155) and the new `ConflictException` in addon.service.ts:143-147 emit no log line. On the client, choose-plan/page.tsx:98 replaces every server message with "Please try again." — the shape lesson L-071 was written about ("the web modal said 'check the file and try again', so it read as a bad file, not a missing entitlement"). Concrete scenario: during the API-deploys-before-web window an ACTIVE tenant on the old bundle posts /billing/subscribe, gets 409 "use upgrade or downgrade to change plan", sees "Could not subscribe. Please try again.", retries forever, and nothing in the API logs or Sentry records that the guard fired.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Log the refusal (tenantId, from/to planKey, cycle) before throwing, as addon.guard.ts does; and surface the server's `message` in the choose-plan error toast instead of the fixed "Please try again." string.

confirmedFindings.summary: `planChangePreview` fetches the full published catalog on every quote although only the UPGRADE branch uses it, doubling the heaviest query on POST /billing/quote.
confirmedFindings.detail: `proration.quote()` already calls `this.catalog.getPublishedCatalog()` (proration.service.ts:74), and `getPublishedCatalog` is uncached — `planVersion.findFirst` with the WITH_CATALOG nested include (plan-catalog.service.ts:60-66, 90-98). The controller now runs both on every quote (settings-billing.controller.ts:84-86), so each plan click and each cycle toggle on /choose-plan issues that query twice, even though `version` is only read in the `rankTo > rankFrom` branch (:355-368) — i.e. never for the SUBSCRIBE / NOOP / DOWNGRADE paths, which include every trial tenant (the common case for this page). The `await` is also sequential, before the Promise.all of the two findUniques.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Move `const version = await this.catalog.getPublishedCatalog();` inside the UPGRADE branch (or pass the version the controller already resolved through `proration.quote` down into `planChangePreview`).

confirmedFindings.summary: The new self-service DOWNGRADE entrance always posts retainedUserIds: [], which makes the period-end cron deactivate every non-admin user when the team exceeds the new seat cap — and no package adds a picker, a warning, or a filed residual for it.
confirmedFindings.detail: dispatchPlanChange() sends {targetPlanKey, retainedUserIds: []} to POST /billing/subscription/downgrade. subscription-mutation.service.ts:447-449 stores that empty array on TenantSubscription.retainedUserIds, and billing-cron.service.ts:168-190 (applyScheduledDowngrades) then does `user.updateMany({ role: {in:[OPERATOR,DRIVER]}, status: ACTIVE, id: { notIn: s.retainedUserIds } }, { status: INACTIVE })` whenever activeTeam > seatCap — the code comment even says "An empty retained list = keep only admins". Scenario: a SCALE tenant with 12 operators/drivers opens /choose-plan, picks GROWTH (seatsIncluded e.g. 5), sees only "Schedule downgrade" and "Takes effect <date>" (choose-plan/page.tsx:222-231 renders no seat copy), clicks once; at period end all 12 operator/driver logins are deactivated. Before this change the chooser never reached the downgrade endpoint at all, so this consequence is newly reachable from self-service. Grep confirms choose-plan is the ONLY web caller of useDowngrade — settings/billing/page.tsx:176-180 only *displays* a pending downgrade — so no sibling UI supplies a retained-seat list either. cause-ruling.md §2 blessed `retainedUserIds: []` and build-plan.md lists a seat picker as a non-goal, but §8's residual list does not include this one, so nothing records it.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Either surface the consequence at the commit point (seat count vs. target plan's seatsIncluded, with a named-user retention step) or make the web call omit retainedUserIds and have downgrade() default to retaining the current in-cap seats; at minimum file it as an explicit residual registry row alongside the other two B58 residuals.

confirmedFindings.summary: Disabling the commit button on NOOP removes the only self-service way to cancel a scheduled downgrade, because subscribe()'s update branch is the sole non-cron writer of downgradeToPlanKey: null.
confirmedFindings.detail: grep for downgradeToPlanKey shows exactly three writers: billing-cron.service.ts:159 (the cron applying it), subscription-mutation.service.ts:447 (scheduling it) and subscription-mutation.service.ts:217 — subscribe()'s upsert `update` branch, which clears `cancelAtPeriodEnd`, `downgradeToPlanKey` and `downgradeEffectiveAt`. That was the only self-service undo: re-picking the current plan in the chooser. planChangePreview() now returns NOOP for same plan + same cycle (subscription-mutation.service.ts:333), and choose-plan/page.tsx:73 returns early plus :234 disables the button ("Current plan"), so the tenant can no longer commit that request. settings/billing/page.tsx has a Resume control for cancelAtPeriodEnd (:159, useResumeSubscription) but only a text line for a pending downgrade (:176-180) — no cancel action anywhere. Scenario: a tenant schedules a downgrade from the new chooser flow, changes their mind, returns to /choose-plan, sees their current plan with a disabled button and no way to undo; at period end the plan drops (and, per the previous finding, seats are freed). The server would still accept the request (same plan → equal planRank → the new 409 guard does not fire).
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Keep the commit path open when the subscription has a pending downgrade/cancel (e.g. classify same-plan+same-cycle as a 'KEEP_CURRENT'/undo action routed to subscribe(), or add an explicit cancel-scheduled-downgrade control in settings/billing).

The retainedUserIds:[] mass-deactivation (#3 and four duplicates) is made visible rather than silent: a seat warning computed server-side with the cron's own activeTeam query and an acknowledgement checkbox on the web; the retained-seat picker stays an owner residual to record at close-out (Option-B). B73's lock is made unconditional by wrapping any non-transactional client in tenantTransaction at syncInvoiceCommission (#4/#17). Wave 2 (after the routing shapes settle) filters the e2e counters to POST, pins the downgrade body, and adds the pre-deploy dispatchPlanChange unit test (#5/#8/#13/#19/#15/#9). #27 is disputed (the probe line does not exist; restore verified), #28 gets a fail-closed rethrow, #29 is deferred as a documented owner tradeoff. disputed.summary: apps/api/src/supplier-statements/supplier-statements.service.ts:435 carries the same defect as the bug being fixed — A DB error in the applied-payment lookup returns `[]`, so `getScan` shows a statement line as having no payments applied and an operator can
disputed.reason: The finding's failure scenario ('an operator can apply a second payment for the same bill; I could not identify any duplicate-payment guard on the apply path') is demonstrably impossible — there are two independent guards on the apply path, plus the response itself contradicts the premise. (1) Same-scan re-apply is refused, twice: apps/api/src/supplier-statements/statement-apply.service.ts:147 `if (scan.status === "APPLIED") { return this.alreadyAppliedResult(scan.appliedPaymentGroupId); }` before the transaction, and again inside it at :192 `await tx.$executeRaw`SELECT id FROM "SupplierStatementScan" WHERE id = ${scanId} FOR UPDATE`` followed by :195 `if (fresh.status === "APPLIED") { return this.alreadyAppliedResult(fresh.appliedPaymentGroupId); }`. So no amount of empty `appliedPayments` in the getScan view lets the same scan write payments a second time. (2) Even from a different scan of the same statement, a duplicate payment for a bill is refused by the ledger-derived remaining-balance guard at statement-apply.service.ts:257-265: `const alreadyPaid = roundMoney(bill.payments.reduce((s, p) => s + Number(p.amount), 0)); const remaining = roundMoney(Number(bill.totalOwed) - alreadyPaid); if (amount > remaining + BALANCE_EPSILON) throw new BadRequestException(`Confirmed amount ... exceeds its remaining balance of ${remaining.toFixed(2)}.`)` — computed from the bill's own BillPayment rows, not from the scan, so it is unaffected by the swallowed lookup; the implied-paid loop repeats the same computation at :337. (3) The premise that getScan 'shows a statement line as having no payments applied' is itself wrong: supplier-statements.service.ts:392-393 still returns `appliedAt: scan.appliedAt ?? null` and `appliedPaymentGroupId: scan.appliedPaymentGroupId ?? null` from the scan row, so an applied scan is still reported as applied even when `fetchAppliedPayments` returns []. The fail-open is also an explicit, documented decision at supplier-statements.service.ts:405 — 'Never throws: the extraction and its matches are what the operator came for, and a failed lookup here must not hide them.' Removing the try/catch per the design would make getScan throw for a scan whose extraction and matches are fine, in a module outside this run's radius, to prevent a money outcome that two guards already prevent.
