remainingFindings.summary: The new inline comment justifying upgrade()'s `!fromKey` clause claims it also catches "a stored key the catalog does not know", which resolveFromPlanKey never produces when a tenant row is loaded — the same class of false in-code assertion the previous round's finding #3 was raised for, now in the opposite direction.
remainingFindings.detail: The comment added at :505-512 reads: "(`!fromKey` retained only for the unrankable residue — no tenant row, or a stored key the catalog does not know — which was refused before this guard existed and narrows the type.)" The second disjunct is false. `resolveFromPlanKey` (:134-136) is `normalizePlanKey(subPlanKey) ?? (tenantPlan ? planKeyFromEnum(tenantPlan) : null)`, and `normalizePlanKey` (plan-catalog.constants.ts:91-98) returns null for any key that is neither in PLAN_KEYS nor an own key of LEGACY_PLAN_KEY_ALIASES — at which point the `??` falls through to `planKeyFromEnum(tenantPlan)`, which has a `default: return "STARTER"` (:173-185). Since `Tenant.plan` is non-nullable, an unknown stored key on a loaded tenant ALWAYS resolves to a key, so `!fromKey` fires only for "no tenant row". The class's own resolveFromPlanKey docblock, rewritten correctly this round at :125-128 ("Null only when there is neither a subscription planKey nor a loaded tenant row"), directly contradicts the new comment 380 lines below it. This is not purely cosmetic: it tells a maintainer that a subscription carrying an unrecognized stored planKey (say a hand-written "PRO") is refused by upgrade(), when in fact it passes every clause — `sub.planKey` is truthy so the ACTIVE-tenant clause is skipped, ranking is done off `Tenant.plan` instead of the stored key, `ledgerOldMonthly` is priced from that resolved key rather than from what the row stores, and the optimistic `where: { tenantId, planKey: sub.planKey }` (:534) still matches, so the upgrade commits. No test covers that shape; I did not find a shipped writer that produces an unrecognized planKey, so this is a comment/documentation defect with a latent behavioural note, not a live money bug.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Trim the parenthetical to the one case that is real — e.g. "(`!fromKey` retained only for the unrankable residue: no tenant row at all — it also narrows the type.)" — or, if the intent is genuinely to refuse an unrecognized stored key, add that as its own clause (`sub.planKey && !normalizePlanKey(sub.planKey)`) with a pin, rather than implying `!fromKey` already does it.

remainingFindings.summary: The new "at most ONE transition is ever armed" invariant enrols every self-service writer but not platform-admin's two plan writers, and this diff creates the first UI that can arm a downgrade schedule.
remainingFindings.detail:
VERIFIED BY READING. The new class docblock on apps/api/src/billing/subscription-mutation.service.ts (line ~96) asserts: "At most ONE transition is ever armed: every committing path clears the markers the others write." upgrade() (:546), downgrade() (:614), cancel(), resume() and subscribe() (:262) were all changed in this diff to clear downgradeToPlanKey / downgradeEffectiveAt / cancelAtPeriodEnd. Two platform-admin writers of the same row were not.

(a) platform-admin.service.ts updatePlan() :436-451 upserts planKey / currentPlan / planVersionId / basePriceSnapshot and leaves downgradeToPlanKey, downgradeEffectiveAt and retainedUserIds untouched.
(b) activateManualSubscription() :516-538 rolls periodStart/periodEnd forward and clears only cancelAtPeriodEnd — downgradeEffectiveAt keeps pointing at the OLD (now past) period end.

Why this is newly reachable, not a dormant hole: `grep -rn "useDowngrade|downgrade.mutate" apps/web` returns ONLY choose-plan/page.tsx (lines 12, 46, 139) — all added by this diff. Before F18 no web surface called POST /billing/subscription/downgrade at all, so downgradeToPlanKey was effectively never armed by a tenant. The new DOWNGRADE routing is the first producer.

Failure scenario: tenant on SCALE, 12 active operators/drivers, schedules a downgrade to STARTER on /choose-plan (downgradeToPlanKey='STARTER', downgradeEffectiveAt=periodEnd, retainedUserIds=[]). They call support; the platform admin PATCHes /platform-admin/tenants/:id/plan back to SCALE (updatePlan). The row still carries the armed downgrade. At 02:00 billing-cron.service.ts applyScheduledDowngrades (:124-125) selects on `downgradeEffectiveAt: { not: null, lte: now }` alone — never on rank or current plan — sets planKey='STARTER', and because retainedUserIds is [] and activeTeam (12) > STARTER's seatCap it runs `user.updateMany({ role: { in: ['OPERATOR','DRIVER'] }, id: { notIn: [] } }, { status: 'INACTIVE' })` (:180-189). Every operator and driver is deactivated and the tenant is dropped off the plan the admin just restored. Same path via activateManualSubscription: the admin renews the period, downgradeEffectiveAt is now in the past, so the very next 02:00 tick fires it.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Clear cancelAtPeriodEnd / downgradeToPlanKey / downgradeEffectiveAt / retainedUserIds in updatePlan()'s upsert `update` branch and in activateManualSubscription()'s, the same way upgrade() (:546) and subscribe() (:262) now do — or narrow the docblock claim and file the two seams explicitly. The ruling's "must not change" list names platform-admin.controller.ts, not the service.
remainingFindings.decision: The diff's own docblock asserts every committing path clears the other transitions' markers, yet platform-admin's updatePlan() and activateManualSubscription() write the same row and leave downgradeToPlanKey/downgradeEffectiveAt armed; with /choose-plan now the first UI that arms a schedule, an admin plan change can be silently overridden by a stale scheduled downgrade at period end. Not a blocker because it needs a tenant-armed schedule followed by an admin write, but it is a real cross-writer hole the invariant claims to close.

remainingFindings.summary: downgrade() and upgrade() now silently revoke a pending cancellation, and planChangePreview surfaces no warning for it — a tenant who cancelled is put back on the hook indefinitely.
remainingFindings.detail:
VERIFIED BY READING THE DIFF. Both `cancelAtPeriodEnd: false` writes are NEW in this change: downgrade() at :614 ("Exactly one transition may be armed: scheduling a downgrade replaces a pending cancellation") and upgrade() at :546. subscribe() has always done it at :262.

planChangePreview sets `warning` in exactly three places: the cycle-switch SUBSCRIBE branch, the KEEP_CURRENT branch ("A scheduled change is pending — keeping your current plan cancels it.") and the DOWNGRADE seat-cap branch (:465-473). The UPGRADE branch (:434-450) and the DOWNGRADE branch (:481-488) return no warning when `cancelAtPeriodEnd` is true, even though planChangePreview already SELECTs `cancelAtPeriodEnd` (:398). The PlanChangePreview interface's own doc for `warning` names "a pending schedule KEEP_CURRENT would cancel" as the motivating case — the same class, implemented for only one of the three branches.

Failure scenario: tenant cancels on /settings/billing (cancelAtPeriodEnd=true; subscription ends at period end, no further charges). Cancelling for price reasons, they then open /choose-plan and pick STARTER. planChangePreview returns { action: 'DOWNGRADE', effectiveAt: periodEnd, proratedNow: null } with no warning. choose-plan/page.tsx renders "Due today $0", "Takes effect <date>" and the button "Schedule downgrade"; nothing says the cancellation is being revoked. downgrade() writes cancelAtPeriodEnd:false, so billing-cron applyScheduledCancellations will never fire and the tenant keeps paying $59/mo forever. The same silent revocation happens through upgrade() (:546) and through a cycle switch on subscribe() (:262). No test in subscription-mutation.service.spec.ts covers the cancellation-armed + different-plan combination — the T10 tests only cover downgrade-armed and the reverse direction.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Add a `warning` to the UPGRADE and DOWNGRADE branches of planChangePreview when priorSub.cancelAtPeriodEnd is true ("your scheduled cancellation will be called off"), and add a spec case; the page already renders preview.change.warning.
remainingFindings.decision: Both cancelAtPeriodEnd:false writes in upgrade()/downgrade() are new, planChangePreview already selects cancelAtPeriodEnd and warns in KEEP_CURRENT, but the UPGRADE/DOWNGRADE branches return no warning — a tenant who cancelled and then picks a plan is re-committed to recurring billing with nothing at the decision point saying so. Money consequence without disclosure; same class as the seat-cap warning the run already required.

remainingFindings.summary: An ENTERPRISE tenant can now self-service downgrade out of a negotiated contract from /choose-plan; the cron then books a POSITIVE MRR delta for it and overwrites the negotiated basePriceSnapshot.
remainingFindings.detail:
VERIFIED BY READING. planChangePreview never screens `isCustom` on either side (unlike subscribe() :141 and upgrade() :514, which both refuse it). planRank('ENTERPRISE')=3 (plan-catalog.constants.ts:100). So an ACTIVE tenant whose stored planKey is 'ENTERPRISE' who picks SCALE on /choose-plan gets rankTo(2) < rankFrom(3) -> action 'DOWNGRADE'; dispatchPlanChange (billing.ts:279) posts /billing/subscription/downgrade; downgrade()'s only rank check is `planRank(targetPlanKey) >= planRank(fromKey)` (:593), which passes, so the schedule is written. This is newly reachable: choose-plan/page.tsx (lines 12/46/139, all added here) is the ONLY web caller of useDowngrade (`grep -rn "useDowngrade|downgrade.mutate" apps/web` confirms).

Money consequence at period end. An ENTERPRISE tenant's negotiated fee lives in priceOverrideMonthly and is back-filled into basePriceSnapshot (platform-admin.service.ts:870-912 documents exactly this); the ENTERPRISE catalog definition has monthlyPrice null. billing-cron.service.ts applyScheduledDowngrades computes `amountDelta = roundMoney(planMonthly(version,'SCALE') - planMonthly(version,'ENTERPRISE'))` (:147-149) and planMonthly returns 0 for a null price -> amountDelta = +499. It then writes `basePriceSnapshot: targetDef.monthlyPrice` = 499 (:158). MrrService prices the snapshot only (mrr.service.ts:80-84), so the run-rate falls 2000 -> 499 (-1501) while the append-only ledger books +499: a permanent ~2000 divergence between `mrr` and `ledgerMrr` from one tenant click — precisely the divergence platform-admin.service.ts:452-456 warns about. priceOverrideMonthly is left at 2000, so the tenant is entitled to SCALE while still priced at the Enterprise fee.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Refuse (or route to "contact sales") when the tenant's current plan definition isCustom — in planChangePreview and in downgrade() — mirroring the isCustom refusals subscribe() and upgrade() already carry.
remainingFindings.decision: planChangePreview never screens isCustom and downgrade()'s only check is rank, so an ENTERPRISE tenant reaches a DOWNGRADE schedule from the new chooser (the only web caller of useDowngrade), and the cron then re-prices from the catalog, overwriting the negotiated basePriceSnapshot and booking a positive MRR delta. subscribe() and upgrade() both refuse isCustom; downgrade() is the odd one out on a newly opened path.

remainingFindings.summary: For a tenant whose stored planKey is a legacy alias, re-picking their own (renamed) plan still routes to subscribe() and resets periodStart/periodEnd — the exact B58 harm — and silently wipes a pending downgrade.
remainingFindings.detail:
VERIFIED BY READING; the behaviour is pinned green by the diff's own PIN T13 test. planChangePreview's `samePlan` compares the STORED key against the requested one (:415), and the equal-rank branch (:429-432) returns SUBSCRIBE. The subscribe() guard (:114-130) requires `planRank(input.planKey) !== planRank(fromKey)`, so an equal-rank pick is not refused.

Failure scenario: an ACTIVE tenant carries planKey='BUSINESS' (LEGACY_PLAN_KEY_ALIASES maps BUSINESS -> SCALE, plan-catalog.constants.ts:84-88); the published catalog exposes 'SCALE'. /choose-plan lists SCALE with no "your current plan" marker, so picking it is a normal click. samePlan is false ('BUSINESS' !== 'SCALE'), so the tenant can never reach NOOP or KEEP_CURRENT from the chooser; ranks are equal, so the preview says SUBSCRIBE and the button reads "Subscribe to Scale". dispatchPlanChange posts /billing/subscribe; subscribe()'s upsert `update` branch (:254-266) writes `periodStart: now, periodEnd: addCycle(now, cycle)` — the renewal date jumps a full cycle and MeterUsage (keyed on periodStart) re-buckets, which is the B58 harm the whole fix exists to prevent — and, at :260-262, clears cancelAtPeriodEnd / downgradeToPlanKey / downgradeEffectiveAt, silently cancelling any pending downgrade with no warning shown. PIN T13 (subscription-mutation.service.spec.ts) asserts only that the upsert runs and planVersionId/planKey are re-pinned; it never asserts periodStart/periodEnd, so nothing catches the reset.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Either omit periodStart/periodEnd from subscribe()'s upsert `update` branch when the prior sub is ACTIVE with a live period (a re-pin should not reset the cycle), or give planChangePreview a distinct equal-rank REPIN action the caller commits through a non-period-resetting write. Ruling Amendment 2 chose SUBSCRIBE here deliberately, so this needs an owner call.
remainingFindings.decision: samePlan compares the stored key ('BUSINESS') to the catalog key ('SCALE') so alias tenants can never hit NOOP/KEEP_CURRENT; equal rank falls to SUBSCRIBE, subscribe()'s guard only refuses on rank inequality, so the period reset (the B58 harm) plus a silent wipe of a pending downgrade is reachable and pinned green by T13. Consistent with the already-confirmed planKey-NULL sibling — the guard keys on the raw stored key instead of the resolved one.

remainingFindings.summary: planChangePreview classifies a custom (ENTERPRISE) target as UPGRADE and returns a NEGATIVE proratedNow, a contract every documented consumer of `change.action` would act on.
remainingFindings.detail:

remainingFindings.summary: commit() now sends the *quote response's* cycle instead of the live cycle toggle, so a commit fired before (or after a failed) re-quote subscribes on the wrong billing cycle.
remainingFindings.detail:
REGRESSION introduced by this diff. Old code (git diff, same file): `subscribe.mutate({ planKey: selected, cycle }, ...)` — `cycle` is the live `React.useState<Cycle>` at line 49. New code: `dispatchPlanChange(preview, ...)` (line 137) and `apps/web/lib/api/billing.ts:282` `mutations.subscribe({ planKey: preview.planKey, cycle: preview.cycle })`. `preview` is the QuoteResult, and `apps/api/src/billing/proration.service.ts:77,131` echoes back the cycle of the REQUEST, so `preview.cycle` is whatever cycle the last *successful* quote was for.

The re-quote on a cycle toggle is fire-and-forget (lines 72-76, `React.useEffect(..., [cycle])` -> `quote.mutate(..., { onSuccess: applyPreview })`, no onError) and the commit button's `disabled` (lines 286-288) is `isCommitting || changeAction === "NOOP" || (needsDowngradeAck && !ackDowngrade)` — `quote.isPending` is deliberately NOT in it (contrast line 218, where the per-plan Choose button IS gated on `quote.isPending && isSel`). The cycle pills (lines ~diff, `onClick={() => setCycle(c)}`) are not disabled either.

Failure scenario: TRIAL tenant on /choose-plan picks SCALE -> quote(MONTHLY) resolves, summary + button render. Tenant clicks the ANNUAL pill, then clicks `Subscribe to Scale` before the ANNUAL quote returns (or the quote 500s — there is no onError, so `preview` is simply never replaced and nothing tells the user). `commit()` -> SUBSCRIBE branch -> POST /billing/subscribe `{planKey:'SCALE', cycle:'MONTHLY'}`. `subscribe()` writes `cycle: 'MONTHLY'`, `periodEnd = addCycle(now,'MONTHLY')` and `basePriceSnapshot`. The tenant selected Annual (10x price, 12-month period) and gets Monthly; the pre-diff code would have sent 'ANNUAL'. The same staleness applies to `preview.planKey` (line 278/280/282) and to `changeAction` itself, e.g. a tenant on ANNUAL SCALE who quotes MONTHLY SCALE (action=SUBSCRIBE + cycle warning), toggles back to ANNUAL, and commits before the re-quote lands: subscribe() resets periodStart/periodEnd onto a MONTHLY cycle — the exact period reset B58 exists to prevent, now via the chooser's own staleness.

The new unit test pins the stale behaviour as correct: apps/web/lib/api/billing.test.ts:67 "routes SUBSCRIBE to the subscribe mutation with the quoted cycle" — so no gate catches this.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Either add `quote.isPending` to the commit button's `disabled` and clear `preview` when `cycle`/`selected` change (so a stale quote can never be committed), or have dispatchPlanChange take the live `{planKey: selected, cycle}` for the SUBSCRIBE branch and assert `preview.planKey === selected && preview.cycle === cycle` before committing.
remainingFindings.decision: The diff replaces the live cycle state with the last successful quote's echoed cycle while leaving the cycle re-quote fire-and-forget (no onError) and the commit button enabled during quote.isPending; a commit after a toggle but before (or after a failed) re-quote subscribes on a cycle the toggle no longer shows. That is a money-path regression introduced by this change, not a pre-existing hazard.

remainingFindings.summary: applyScheduledDowngrades has no tenant status / deletedAt filter, so a churned, suspended or soft-deleted tenant's armed downgrade still fires and books a second MRR delta on top of the churn delta.
remainingFindings.detail:
Line 124-125: `where: { downgradeEffectiveAt: { not: null, lte: now }, downgradeToPlanKey: { not: null } }` — no `tenant: { status: ..., deletedAt: null }`. Its two siblings in the same file both have one: `applyScheduledCancellations` (line ~219) filters `tenant: { status: "ACTIVE", deletedAt: null }`, and `expireTrials` (line ~57) filters `deletedAt: null`. The sweep then unconditionally rewrites `planKey`, `currentPlan`, `basePriceSnapshot`, `Tenant.plan`, deactivates OPERATOR/DRIVER rows, and emits PLAN_CHANGED with `amountDelta` (lines 150-208).

This was inert before this diff because nothing in the product armed `downgradeToPlanKey`: `git grep -n 'useDowngrade' HEAD -- apps/web` returns nothing outside lib/api/billing, and a repo-wide grep for `subscription/downgrade` finds only the controller, the specs and the new chooser code. This change is the first product caller, so the filter gap becomes live with it.

Failure scenario: ACTIVE tenant on SCALE ($499) uses the new chooser to schedule a downgrade to STARTER ($99) effective 2026-10-01 (their periodEnd). On 2026-09-20 their card fails; `billing.service.ts` `suspendOverdueTenants` books the churn via `transitionAndEmit(..., -1, SUBSCRIPTION_SUSPENDED)` = -(499 + addons - discount) and sets status SUSPENDED. On 2026-10-01 at 02:00 `applyScheduledDowngrades` still selects the row (no status filter), applies the downgrade to a non-paying tenant and emits PLAN_CHANGED `amountDelta = roundMoney(99 - 499) = -400`. MRR is Sigma(amountDelta) per the service docblock, so the rollup now understates the run-rate by $400 permanently and never self-heals. Same double-book via `onSubscriptionDeleted` (status CANCELLED, -MRR emitted) followed by the 02:00 sweep, and the same sweep will deactivate a soft-deleted tenant's operators/drivers.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Add `tenant: { status: "ACTIVE", deletedAt: null }` to the where-clause (matching applyScheduledCancellations), and decide explicitly what should happen to a schedule left on a tenant that stopped paying — most likely clear the markers rather than apply them.
remainingFindings.decision: applyScheduledDowngrades queries only on the marker fields while both siblings in the same file filter on tenant status/deletedAt, and this change is the first product path that arms those markers — so a churned or soft-deleted tenant's schedule now fires, rewrites the plan row, deactivates staff and books a second MRR delta over the churn delta. Newly reachable, therefore in scope.

remainingFindings.summary: activateManualSubscription (and updatePlan) reset the billing period / plan without clearing downgradeToPlanKey, downgradeEffectiveAt or retainedUserIds, so the 02:00 cron silently reverses the admin's action and can deactivate every operator and driver.
remainingFindings.detail:
`activateManualSubscription` (lines 516-538) upserts `periodStart: now`, `periodEnd: now + billingPeriodDays`, and explicitly `cancelAtPeriodEnd: false` — it disarms ONE transition and leaves the other three fields (`downgradeToPlanKey`, `downgradeEffectiveAt`, `retainedUserIds`) untouched. `updatePlan` (lines 436-450) writes `currentPlan`, `planKey`, `planVersionId`, `basePriceSnapshot` and emits its own PLAN_CHANGED, and clears nothing at all.

The new code asserts the opposite as an invariant: apps/api/src/billing/subscription-mutation.service.ts:99-100 — "At most ONE transition is ever armed: every committing path clears the markers the others write." These two platform-admin writers are committing paths that do not.

Failure scenario (activateManualSubscription): tenant on SCALE schedules a downgrade to STARTER through the new chooser -> `downgradeToPlanKey='STARTER'`, `downgradeEffectiveAt = 2026-10-01`, `retainedUserIds = []` (billing.ts:280 always sends `[]`). The tenant then pays by bank transfer and an admin runs manual activation on 2026-10-05: `periodStart = 2026-10-05`, `periodEnd = 2026-11-05`, `cancelAtPeriodEnd=false`, status ACTIVE. `downgradeEffectiveAt` is still 2026-10-01 — now in the PAST. At the next 02:00 tick `applyScheduledDowngrades` matches (`lte: now`), overwrites `planKey`/`Tenant.plan` to STARTER, rewrites `basePriceSnapshot` to 99, emits PLAN_CHANGED, and — because `retainedUserIds` is `[]` and the team exceeds STARTER's `seatsIncluded` — `updateMany` sets every ACTIVE OPERATOR and DRIVER to INACTIVE (lines 166-197). The admin has no surface that shows or clears the armed schedule.

Same shape via updatePlan: support moves a tenant back up to SCALE after they change their mind; the stale schedule drops them to STARTER at 02:00 on the effective date and books a second PLAN_CHANGED delta against the admin's own.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Clear `downgradeToPlanKey`, `downgradeEffectiveAt` and `retainedUserIds` alongside `cancelAtPeriodEnd: false` in activateManualSubscription's update branch, and in updatePlan's subscription upsert; or centralise a `disarmScheduledTransitions(tx, tenantId)` helper the invariant docblock can actually point at.
remainingFindings.decision: The new service states the invariant 'every committing path clears the markers the others write', and activateManualSubscription/updatePlan are committing writers that clear at most cancelAtPeriodEnd; an armed chooser downgrade survives an admin re-plan and the 02:00 cron reverses it and deactivates OPERATOR/DRIVER rows. Real by the change's own contract.

remainingFindings.summary: The Stripe webhook writers arm cancelAtPeriodEnd without clearing the downgrade markers (and overwrite cancelAtPeriodEnd on every subscription.updated), breaking the exact both-armed hazard cancel()'s own docblock defends against.
remainingFindings.detail:
`onSubscriptionDeleted` (lines 644-682) ends with `this.prisma.tenantSubscription.update({ ..., data: { cancelAtPeriodEnd: true } })` and never touches `downgradeToPlanKey`/`downgradeEffectiveAt`/`retainedUserIds`. `onSubscriptionUpdated` (lines 684-703) writes `periodStart`, `periodEnd` and `cancelAtPeriodEnd: subscription.cancel_at_period_end` on every `customer.subscription.updated` and likewise never touches the downgrade markers.

The self-service twin knows this is dangerous: subscription-mutation.service.ts `cancel()` lines 635-644 clear `downgradeToPlanKey`/`downgradeEffectiveAt`/`retainedUserIds` with the comment "A cancellation SUPERSEDES any scheduled downgrade — leaving one armed would let applyScheduledDowngrades re-price the row (rewriting basePriceSnapshot) before applyScheduledCancellations books the churn delta from it, so the negative MRR delta would depend on which cron ran first." The Stripe path leaves precisely that hole, and it is only now reachable because this diff is the first product caller of downgrade().

Failure scenario A (both armed): tenant on SCALE schedules a downgrade to STARTER for 2026-10-01 via the chooser. On 2026-09-20 Stripe deletes the subscription -> `onSubscriptionDeleted` sets tenant CANCELLED, books -(basePriceSnapshot 499 + addons - discount) once, and sets `cancelAtPeriodEnd: true` on a row that still carries `downgradeToPlanKey='STARTER'`. On 2026-10-01 `applyScheduledDowngrades` (no status filter — see the sibling finding) rewrites `basePriceSnapshot` to 99 and books another PLAN_CHANGED delta of -400 for a tenant already churned.

Failure scenario B (the new KEEP_CURRENT classifier): `planChangePreview` (lines 379-412) keys KEEP_CURRENT on `priorSub.downgradeToPlanKey != null || priorSub.cancelAtPeriodEnd`. Because `onSubscriptionUpdated` overwrites `cancelAtPeriodEnd` from Stripe's value on any subscription update (a cycle roll, a price sync, an item add from addon.service), a tenant who cancelled through RouteFlow can have the flag silently flipped back to false — the settings page's cancellation banner and the chooser's "Keep current plan" undo both disappear, and the cancellation is never applied.
remainingFindings.fixHint: In onSubscriptionDeleted, clear downgradeToPlanKey/downgradeEffectiveAt/retainedUserIds in the same update that sets cancelAtPeriodEnd. For onSubscriptionUpdated, decide whether Stripe is authoritative for cancelAtPeriodEnd at all (a locally-scheduled cancel is not represented in Stripe), and at minimum do not silently clear a locally-armed flag.
remainingFindings.decision: onSubscriptionDeleted arms cancelAtPeriodEnd and onSubscriptionUpdated overwrites it from Stripe on every event, neither touching the downgrade markers — recreating exactly the both-armed, cron-order-dependent MRR delta that cancel()'s docblock says it clears the markers to prevent, and letting Stripe re-arm a cancellation that downgrade()/upgrade() just disarmed.

remainingFindings.summary: For a custom-priced (ENTERPRISE) source the new DOWNGRADE route promises "$0 due today" while the period-end cron books a POSITIVE MRR delta and leaves priceOverrideMonthly in place, so the tenant keeps being billed the enterprise rate on the cheaper plan.
remainingFindings.detail:
An ACTIVE tenant on ENTERPRISE (planKey='ENTERPRISE', `basePriceSnapshot`/`priceOverrideMonthly` = their negotiated fee, e.g. 2000 — see platform-admin.service.ts:417 `definition.monthlyPrice ?? priorSub?.priceOverrideMonthly ?? null`) picks SCALE on /choose-plan. `planChangePreview` reaches the DOWNGRADE branch (rank 3 -> 2) and returns `proratedNow: null, effectiveAt: periodEnd`; the page renders "Due today $0" (choose-plan/page.tsx summary, `changeAction === 'DOWNGRADE' ? 0 : ...`) and "Takes effect <date>". `downgrade()` (lines 571-626) has no isCustom guard and schedules it.

Then billing-cron.service.ts `applyScheduledDowngrades`:
- line 150-153: `amountDelta = roundMoney(this.planMonthly(version,'SCALE') - this.planMonthly(version,'ENTERPRISE'))`. `planMonthly` (lines 46-50) returns 0 when `monthlyPrice == null`, and ENTERPRISE is `isCustom` with a NULL catalog price — so the ledger receives **+499 on a downgrade** instead of -1501. Sigma(amountDelta) overstates MRR by ~$2,000 permanently.
- line 158: `basePriceSnapshot: targetDef?.monthlyPrice ?? null` overwrites 2000 with 499, so the MRR snapshot now prices the tenant at 499.
- Nothing on this path clears `priceOverrideMonthly`. Both price resolvers prefer it: subscription.service.ts:43-47 (`monthlyPrice = sub.priceOverrideMonthly ?? def.monthlyPrice`) and platform-pricing.service.ts:93-115 (`if (overrideMonthly != null ...) return { monthly: overrideMonthly, source: 'override' }`, which is what drives Stripe price sync).

Net: after the downgrade applies, /settings/billing shows the tenant $2,000/mo on the SCALE plan, `resolveTenantPricing` keeps returning 2000, the MRR snapshot says 499, and the ledger moved +499. The chooser told them $0 due today and a move to the $499 plan.

Honest scoping: subscribe() had the same +delta arithmetic (line 307 nets against `oldPlanMonthly` = 0 for ENTERPRISE) and also never cleared the override, so the arithmetic error is not newly introduced. What IS new is that this route affirmatively renders "$0 due today / takes effect <date>" for a custom-priced tenant, and that the change moves this traffic onto the cron path, which additionally rewrites basePriceSnapshot away from the negotiated fee.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Refuse a plan change out of a custom/isCustom plan self-service (route to sales, like subscribe()/upgrade() already do for isCustom targets), or make the cron price the source from `basePriceSnapshot`/`priceOverrideMonthly` when the catalog has no monthlyPrice and clear `priceOverrideMonthly` when leaving a custom plan.
remainingFindings.decision: For an isCustom ENTERPRISE source the DOWNGRADE branch has no guard, the preview promises $0 due today, and the cron's planMonthly(ENTERPRISE) is 0 (null catalog price) so amountDelta is booked positive while priceOverrideMonthly is left in place — the ledger and the tenant's actual charge both go wrong. Money-path defect on a route this change opened.

remainingFindings.summary: The DOWNGRADE and UPGRADE preview branches silently revoke a pending cancellation, while the KEEP_CURRENT branch one block above warns for the identical state.
remainingFindings.detail:
`planChangePreview` selects `cancelAtPeriodEnd` (line 380) and uses it in exactly one of its four branches: the same-plan KEEP_CURRENT branch (line 404-411) returns `warning: "A scheduled change is pending — keeping your current plan cancels it."`. The UPGRADE branch (434-450) and the DOWNGRADE branch (452-488) never look at it, yet both committing paths disarm it: `upgrade()` line 546 `cancelAtPeriodEnd: false` (comment lines 541-545) and `downgrade()` line 614 `cancelAtPeriodEnd: false` (comment lines 612-613 "scheduling a downgrade replaces a pending cancellation rather than stacking on top of it").

Failure scenario: a tenant cancels from /settings/billing (`cancel()` sets `cancelAtPeriodEnd: true`; tenant stays ACTIVE until `applyScheduledCancellations` runs at period end). Before that date they visit /choose-plan to compare, decide to "downgrade instead of leaving" is not what they want, or simply click the cheaper plan to see the price and then commit. The button reads "Schedule downgrade", the preview shows no warning, and the success toast says "Downgrade scheduled — You'll move to the Starter plan at the end of your current cycle" — none of which says the cancellation is now void. `downgrade()` sets `cancelAtPeriodEnd: false`, `applyScheduledCancellations` will never fire, and the tenant is billed on the cheaper plan indefinitely believing they had cancelled. The identical silent revocation happens on the UPGRADE branch.

The code already has the warning mechanism and the state in hand — it is applied to one branch of four.
remainingFindings.fixHint: In planChangePreview, attach a warning to the UPGRADE and DOWNGRADE branches too when `priorSub.cancelAtPeriodEnd` (or a differing `downgradeToPlanKey`) is armed, e.g. "Your scheduled cancellation will be cancelled" — and consider gating the commit behind the same acknowledgement checkbox the seat warning uses.
remainingFindings.decision: KEEP_CURRENT warns that committing cancels a pending change but the UPGRADE and DOWNGRADE branches, which both set cancelAtPeriodEnd:false on commit, say nothing; the state is identical and the warning belongs on all three. Real inconsistency at the point of decision, but the commit outcome (keep the subscription) is the plausible intent, so minor.

remainingFindings.summary: A published plan key outside PLAN_KEYS ranks -1, so the preview classifies it as a DOWNGRADE from every plan, downgrade() accepts it, and the cron then writes basePriceSnapshot: null — where the old subscribe() route priced it correctly.
remainingFindings.detail:
`planRank` (plan-catalog.constants.ts:101-104) returns -1 for any key `normalizePlanKey` cannot resolve (not in `PLAN_KEYS = [STARTER, GROWTH, SCALE, ENTERPRISE]` and not in `LEGACY_PLAN_KEY_ALIASES = {TEAM, BUSINESS, PROFESSIONAL}`). The published catalog is DATA (a PlanVersion published by `db:publish:catalog:v11`); I found no code path that constrains a published `PlanDefinition.planKey` to PLAN_KEYS.

So the day a catalog version publishes a plan key that was not also added to PLAN_KEYS (say 'PRO'), the chooser lists it (usePlans -> /billing/plans) and:
- planChangePreview line 427-433: `rankTo = -1 < rankFrom` for every existing plan -> DOWNGRADE, unconditionally.
- downgrade() line 593: `planRank('PRO') >= planRank(from)` is `-1 >= 0..3` = false -> accepted; `def` IS found in the published catalog so the earlier check passes. The schedule is written.
- billing-cron applyScheduledDowngrades line 149-158: `findPlanDefinition(pinnedVersion, 'PRO')` normalizes to 'PRO' and finds nothing in an older pinned version -> `targetDef === undefined` -> `basePriceSnapshot: null` and `amountDelta = 0 - oldMonthly`; `planKeyToEnum('PRO')` (constants:199-210) falls through to 'STARTER' for `currentPlan` and `Tenant.plan`. The tenant lands on a plan with a NULL base price — `MrrService` prices from the snapshot, so they are free.

Before this diff the same pick went through subscribe(), which reads `def` from the PUBLISHED catalog and writes `basePriceSnapshot: def.monthlyPrice` — the correct price. The new B58 guard (line 187, `planRank(input.planKey) !== planRank(fromKey)`) additionally now 409s that path for an ACTIVE tenant, so the correct route is closed and only the broken one is open. Reachability depends on an operational mistake (publishing an off-list key), which is why I am scoring this minor rather than major.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Reject an unrankable key explicitly rather than letting -1 mean "lowest": in planChangePreview return SUBSCRIBE (or throw) when `planRank(planKey) < 0`, and in downgrade() refuse when either rank is -1. A catalog-publish-time assertion that every definition's planKey normalizes into PLAN_KEYS would close it at the source.
remainingFindings.decision: planRank returns -1 for an unknown key and neither planChangePreview nor downgrade() rejects a negative rank, so a published key outside PLAN_KEYS is classified DOWNGRADE from every plan and the cron writes basePriceSnapshot null where subscribe() used to price it. Contingent on a future catalog publish, but a negative-rank guard is the cheap correct fix and the evidence is not refuted; kept as minor.
